angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 862,668 km at 103.90 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.6247 +/- 0.0199 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 103.90 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.24 +/- 0.07 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1716.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract): 862,668 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.07 +/- 0.14 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1716.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5879 +/- 141 K from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1716.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1716.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1716.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.281, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
